Long-form correspondence from across the foundry — written from the marsh edge, the seed bench, the auditor's table. We post slowly, in season, and only when there is something worth recording.

saltmarsh
Three years on, the Cardigan Bay saltmarsh is holding sediment faster than projected.

The third year of monitoring across plots 8a through 8d shows mean accretion of 12.4 mm/yr — well above the 7 mm/yr modelled in the 2022 prospectus. We walk through the surveys, what the cores tell us, and why we are revising the carbon ledger upward for this site.

BY ELIN MAREK · AUDITOR: R. OHENE · 11 MIN READ

FIELD NOTE
· HEN HARRIERS
· 09 MAY 2026
Beaver dam analogues at Glyn Lewes: first measurable channel widening.

Eight months after we installed the BDAs above the confluence, we are seeing the channel begin to widen on its own. Notes from a slow walk along the bank with the upland team.

THEIA ROURKE
· 7 MIN

· 28 APR 2026
From the Carpathian foot: thirty hectares of elm growth bench under greater protection.

The Romanian forestry partnership extended its lease and the elm regeneration cohort is now fully enrolled in the long-term inventory. We share the quarterly read.

IULIA PANAS
· 12 MIN

FIELD NOTE
· METHODS

Year-three serviced audit, Loch Awe planting: 16.4% across 142,000 stems.

Survival rate after three winters of monitoring, broken down by exposure, soil type, and the slow march of the deer fence. Cautious optimism on the south slopes.

Donation reconciliation, august 2025: 4,214 contributions matched, 12 pending review.

How the matching engine resolved the giving month — what we caught, what we forwarded to the auditor, and why two larger gifts are still in the queue.

Peat re-wetting at border Mires: water table holding within 6 cm of surface for 218 of 240 monitored days.

The cross-border peatland is meeting its hydrological targets in the first full year. Submitting a short note in support of the DEFRA consultation.

PAST NOTES BY THE SEASON
2021 — 2026 · 72 ENTRIES INDEXED
21 — 03
Three sample lowlands, four 8 m delerigated.
The southwestern lowlands moved to permanent rotation. Surveyed by Theia R. and the Glyn Lewes crew during a wet March.
21 — 06
Hindwarbler, 142,000 in transplanted from Saxonist sed-bench.
The first big move of nursery stock onto the upland enclosures. A note on logistics, fence permits, and what we will do differently next year.
22 — 02
Stayed by 80 millimetre of receivable after the summer gales.
The Cardigan Bay sediment record held through a violent August. We re-cored the four plots and added a fifth.
22 — 08
Border wires Equest closes — the foundry steps in.
When the Border Mires consortium dissolved, we picked up the lease on the two main bog blocks. What that meant for the donor ledger.
23 — 04
First re-wetting at Border Mires: water table holding within 8 cm.
First good seasonal hold. We are cautious; the data is encouraging but we have one more summer to go before we will use the word "stable" in print.
